name: sandbox

frames.best_why: Frame 1 shows the full shell: tab bar, file tree and syntax-highlighted editor together.

tagline: Code, preview and console share one window with a file tree and editor.
summary: A full in-browser code playground: a file list beside an editor, plus Preview and Console tabs, so a snippet can be edited and run without leaving the page.
appearance: A near-full-width dark panel with a header of three small tabs (Code, Preview, Console) above a body. On Code, a narrow file list sits left of a syntax-highlighted editor; Preview shows a plain app page with a heading and three rows.
behaviour: Tapping a tab swaps the body: Code shows the file tree and editor, Preview renders the running app, Console lists its logs. The active tab gets a lighter pill and the old pane fades out quickly.
demo_content: A task list app headed 'Today' with three tasks: Write release notes, Review PR #482, Book flights to Lisbon.
search_phrases: run react snippets in the browser
editor with preview and console tabs
edit and preview components side by side
use_when: Documentation or a tutorial needs a runnable example that readers can edit and preview on the page itself.
avoid_when: It loads a remote bundler and several panes, so it is heavy for a landing page and needs a network to run code.
customise: Files, template and theme pass through to the sandbox provider; tab labels, panel chrome and which panes appear are set by composing the exported pieces.
weight_why: Loads the Sandpack bundler and runs the preview in an iframe, so startup and memory cost are real.

a11y.note: Tabs expose roles and aria-selected but are not linked to their panels with aria-controls, and the file tree is not described.

issues: The console text is so dim against the dark panel that the log lines are hard to read.
polish_why: The shell and editor look tidy, but the console is almost illegible and the preview page is plain.
